standard_prerequisites.name: For a system of complexes indexed by the natural numbers the termwise colimit fits into a short exact sequence from the countable sum to itself given by the shifts of the transition maps
standard_prerequisites.use: Displays the sequence whose associated triangle expresses the colimit in terms of the countable sum.

standard_prerequisites.name: The shift of a morphism of complexes defines a distinguished triangle in the derived category
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the displayed short exact sequence into a distinguished triangle, which is what allows a long exact sequence to be written.

standard_prerequisites.name: The functor represented by a fixed object of the derived category is homological, so a distinguished triangle yields a long exact sequence of abelian groups
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the displayed long exact sequence from which the conclusion is read.

core_obligations: Consider the short exact sequence of complexes from the countable sum of the system to itself given in degree n by one minus the transition map, with the termwise colimit as quotient, and record that it defines a distinguished triangle in the derived category (proof lines 20347-20356).

Apply the homological functor represented by the fixed object to that triangle and write the resulting long exact sequence in the displayed diagram, identifying the value on the colimit with the colimit of the values on the terms (proof lines 20356-20362).

Use the countable sum hypothesis to identify the value of the functor on the countable sum with the countable sum of the values on the individual terms, and conclude that the first map in each row, namely the sum of the maps induced by one minus the transition maps, is injective (proof lines 20363-20369).

Read off from the exactness of the middle row that the value of the functor on the termwise colimit is the cokernel of that injective map, which is exactly the colimit of the values, and conclude the bijectivity asserted in the statement (proof lines 20369-20375).
proof_roadmap: Display the short exact sequence relating the countable sum, its shift by the transition maps and the termwise colimit, and lift it to a distinguished triangle (proof lines 20347-20356).
Apply the represented functor and write the long exact sequence (proof lines 20356-20362).
Use the hypothesis to see that the first map is injective and conclude that the functor on the colimit is the colimit of the values (proof lines 20363-20375).
difficulty_reason: The statement assumes that a fixed object of the derived category commutes with countable direct sums in the sense that the canonical map on Hom groups is a bijection, and concludes that it likewise commutes with the termwise colimit of any countable system of complexes (statement lines 20331-20345). The proof encodes the colimit of a countable system as the quotient of the countable sum by the image of the shift of the transition maps, upgrades that short exact sequence to a distinguished triangle, applies the represented homological functor and uses the hypothesis to see that the first map of the resulting long exact sequence is injective, which identifies the value on the colimit with the colimit of the values (proof lines 20347-20375). The comparison of the countable sum with the termwise colimit through the transition maps is the technical device that makes the statement work. The counted span refers twice to results of another chapter, both carried as navigation stubs.
